name: Cefradine

overview.mechanism: A beta-lactam antibacterial that acts on penicillin-binding proteins involved in bacterial cell-wall synthesis.
uses: Historical clinical and pharmacokinetic literature also uses the spelling cephradine. Current indication and dosing must come from the specific Philippine product insert.

paragraphs.text: A 1990 study compared 10 healthy young volunteers with nine older adults after IV and oral cephradine. Systemic and renal clearance were lower in the older group, and systemic clearance correlated with creatinine clearance. More than 80% of the dose was recovered in urine within six hours in both groups.

After IV administration, mean elimination half-life was 1.71 hours in older participants versus 1.12 hours in younger participants. These small-group pharmacokinetic observations describe an exposure difference; they do not establish a modern CKD, HD or CRRT regimen.

A historical study in noninfected CAPD patients found that oral cephradine produced dialysate concentrations inadequate against Staphylococcus epidermidis and most gram-negative bacteria associated with CAPD peritonitis. This pharmacokinetic finding is not a current treatment recommendation for PD-associated peritonitis.
